ai_tools.name: Avoca AI
ai_tools.tagline: AI call answering, outbound follow-up and call coaching for home-service companies
ai_tools.pricing_summary: No public pricing; quoted after a demo with Avoca's sales team
ai_tools.long_description:
Avoca builds AI agents for service businesses that answer calls, texts and web chats, book jobs, run outbound campaigns and score calls made by a company's own customer service reps (CSRs). Its website lists HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing, garage door, restoration, pest control and several other service industries, and its April 2026 press release names Turnpoint, 1-800-GOT-JUNK? and Goettl as customers.

The company was founded in 2022 by Tyson Chen and Apurva Shrivastava and went through Y Combinator's Winter 2023 batch. According to Fortune, the founders first built call answering for restaurants and moved into home services after building a product for Rescue Air, a Dallas HVAC company, in 2023. Avoca is based in New York with an office in Santa Barbara.

In April 2026 Avoca announced it had raised more than $125 million across Seed, Series A and Series B at a $1 billion valuation. Kleiner Perkins led the Series A, and Meritech and General Catalyst led the Series B.

The product is split into Convert (inbound calls, texts and chat, with 24/7 booking), Nurture (SMS and call drip campaigns to past customers), Coach (every call scored 0-100 against your own rubric) and add-ons such as Speed-to-Lead, Web Chat and Google Local Services Ads handling. Avoca lists ServiceTitan (as a certified app), Housecall Pro and FieldRoutes as integrations.

The trade-off: Avoca publishes no prices, so you only learn the cost after a demo with its sales team, and its customer list and feature set point to multi-truck operations rather than a one-person shop.
ai_tools.how_it_works: You start by booking a demo with Avoca; there is no public price list or self-serve plan on its website. Avoca connects to your field service software (it lists ServiceTitan, Housecall Pro and FieldRoutes) so the AI can book jobs straight into your schedule. Convert answers inbound calls, texts and web chats 24/7. Speed-to-Lead picks up new leads from sources such as web forms, Google Local Services Ads, Facebook, Yelp and Angi, and Avoca says it responds in under 5 seconds. Nurture runs SMS and call campaigns to re-engage past customers. Coach scores every call, including your human CSRs' calls, from 0 to 100 against your own rubric and flags missed opportunities for managers.

cons_detail.explanation: The named customers (Turnpoint, 1-800-GOT-JUNK?, Goettl) and the outbound and coaching features point to multi-truck companies; a solo operator will likely pay for more than they use.

ai_tools.name: Rosie
ai_tools.tagline: AI answering service for small service businesses from $49/mo
ai_tools.pricing_summary: Professional $49/mo (250 minutes); Scale $149/mo (1,000 minutes, calendar booking and call transfers); Growth $299/mo (2,000 minutes, custom agent training). Annual billing gives 2 months free. 7-day free trial. US and Canada only
ai_tools.long_description:
Rosie is an AI answering service for small businesses that miss calls while they are working. Its website has pages for home services, plumbing and construction alongside law firms, property management, real estate, automotive and salons, so it is a general small-business tool with trade-friendly features rather than a trades-only product. Rosie says more than 2,000 businesses use it.

Rosie answers 24/7 in English and Spanish. During setup it scans your website and Google Business Profile to learn your hours, services and basic details, and you then add FAQs and test its answers before forwarding your calls. Every plan includes call summaries, transcripts and recordings, spam detection, a website chat widget, iOS and Android apps and a Zapier connection.

The plans differ by minutes and features. Professional ($49/mo) includes 250 minutes, message taking and appointment links sent by text. Scale ($149/mo) includes 1,000 minutes, books directly on your calendar, and adds warm and live call transfers and texting during the call. Growth ($299/mo) includes 2,000 minutes, waterfall transfers, custom agent training, white-glove onboarding and priority support. Paying annually gives 2 months free, and there is a 7-day free trial.

Rosie is operated by Rally Commerce, Inc., which founder Jordan Gal pivoted from an e-commerce checkout business in 2024. Its terms limit the service to the United States and Canada, and its help center says accounts get US phone numbers only.

The trade-off: direct calendar booking and call transfers start at the $149 Scale plan, the minute allowances are fixed per plan, and the product is a young one built for many kinds of small business rather than for trades alone.
ai_tools.how_it_works: You sign up for the 7-day free trial and Rosie scans your website and Google Business Profile to learn your hours, services and basic information. You review what it learned, add FAQs and test its answers, then set up call forwarding to your Rosie number. Rosie answers in English or Spanish, takes messages based on scenarios you set, and sends callers appointment links by text. On Scale and up it books directly into Google Calendar, Calendly, Acuity or Appointlet and can transfer live calls to your team. You get call summaries, transcripts and recordings in the app, and Rosie's help center has integration guides for field service software such as Jobber, Housecall Pro and Workiz, plus Zapier for other tools.

ai_tools.name: Goodcall
ai_tools.tagline: Self-serve AI phone agent for small businesses, priced per agent with unlimited minutes
ai_tools.pricing_summary: Starter $79/mo per agent (100 unique callers/month); Growth $129/mo (250); Scale $249/mo (500). About 15% less billed annually ($66/$108/$208). Unlimited minutes; $0.50 per extra unique caller. Enterprise pricing is custom
ai_tools.long_description:
Goodcall is a self-serve AI phone agent for small and mid-size businesses. You set up an agent that answers inbound customer-service and sales calls, collects caller details and books appointments, and Goodcall says you can launch one in a few minutes with no engineering team. It says more than 42,000 businesses use it, and its own industry pages focus on salons, healthcare and call centers rather than trades.

Goodcall traces its roots to Google: its about page says a Google Ads team spotted the problem in 2017, the idea became CallJoy inside Google's Area 120 incubator, and Goodcall later spun out as its own company. The operating company is Goodcall AI Inc. of Palo Alto, California, and its named investors include Neo, Foothill Ventures, Merus Capital and Xoogler Ventures.

Pricing is per agent: Starter $79/mo, Growth $129/mo and Scale $249/mo, or $66, $108 and $208 a month billed annually. Minutes are unlimited, but each plan includes a set number of unique callers per month (100, 250 or 500), and each extra unique caller costs $0.50. A caller who phones many times in a month counts once, and robocalls, blocked numbers and callers who never speak do not count. Higher plans add more call-flow logic, team members and call history.

The agent syncs with your CRM and calendar (Google Calendar is named) to book appointments, and it shares every call's details by SMS, email, Google Sheets or your CRM. Goodcall lists SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 and HIPAA compliance.

The trade-off: Goodcall is a general small-business tool with no trade-specific setup, the cheapest plan covers only 100 unique callers a month, and there is no published free trial beyond a free demo plan without a phone number.
ai_tools.how_it_works: You sign up on Goodcall's website and build an AI agent yourself: you connect your knowledge sources and business tools, write the greeting and set up call-flow logic (the number of logic flows depends on your plan). You then connect your calendar and CRM so the agent can find open times and book appointments, and choose where call details go: SMS, email, Google Sheets or your CRM, with Zapier for other apps. Goodcall gives you a local phone number, which you publish or forward calls to. The agent answers, handles customer-service and sales questions and logs each call. Billing counts unique callers per month rather than minutes, and a free Demo plan lets one user try the agent without a live phone number.

ai_tools.tagline: AI receptionist with a free plan, plus human-first live receptionists answering 24/7
ai_tools.pricing_summary: AI Receptionist: Free (25 calls/mo, then $3.00/call), Pro $150/mo ($2.00/call), Enterprise $500/mo ($1.67/call). Human-first receptionists: $300/mo for 30 calls, $810/mo for 90, $2,100/mo for 300 (overage $8.50-$11.50/call). No setup fees, month-to-month; 30-day money-back guarantee on receptionist plans
ai_tools.long_description:
Smith.ai sells two phone-answering services: a self-serve AI Receptionist and a Human-first Virtual Receptionist service in which live, North America-based receptionists answer every call with AI guidance in the background. Co-founders Aaron Lee (a former CTO of The Home Depot) and Justin Maxwell started the company in 2015, and it says it has handled more than 25 million calls. Its website leads with law firms, with home services listed among its other industries.

The AI Receptionist answers 24/7 in English or Spanish, qualifies leads, routes calls, books appointments through Calendly and other schedulers, and records, transcribes and summarizes each call. The Free plan covers 25 calls a month and then charges $3.00 per call, Pro is $150/mo at $2.00 per call, and Enterprise is $500/mo at $1.67 per call with full-service setup and multi-location support. You can add live receptionists from Smith.ai's network for calls that need a person, billed per call.

The Human-first plans cost $300/mo for 30 calls, $810/mo for 90 calls and $2,100/mo for 300 calls, with overage of $11.50, $10.50 or $8.50 per call. Spam calls are not charged, there are no setup fees, service is month-to-month, and a 12-month commitment takes 10% off. New clients get a 30-day money-back guarantee on the plan and add-ons, up to $1,000, excluding overage.

The trade-off: Smith.ai bills per call rather than per minute, so a busy shop needs to model its monthly call count, and live human coverage costs far more than the AI plans. It is also a general business service focused mostly on law firms rather than a trades-specific tool.
ai_tools.how_it_works: For the AI Receptionist, you sign up online (a card is required even for the free plan, with no charge until you authorize one), test the agent in Smith.ai's Quality Studio, then forward your calls to the dedicated number it gives you. The AI answers 24/7 in English or Spanish, qualifies leads, answers questions from your FAQs, routes calls and books appointments through Calendly or other connected schedulers, and sends you recordings, transcripts and summaries. It connects to CRMs such as Salesforce and HubSpot natively, or to other apps through Zapier and Make. For the Human-first service, you pick a plan by monthly call count and Smith.ai's live receptionists answer every call around the clock, screening leads, booking appointments and taking payments by your instructions. Both services bill per call, not per minute.

ai_tools.name: Hover
ai_tools.tagline: 3D models, measurements, design and estimates from smartphone photos
ai_tools.pricing_summary: Current prices could not be verified (Hover's pricing page blocked automated reading); confirm with Hover. Instant Design is free for homeowners and includes up to five free projects a year for pros
ai_tools.long_description:
Hover turns smartphone photos of a home into a measured 3D model that contractors use to order materials, design the job with the homeowner and build an estimate. It started with exteriors (roofing, siding, windows and gutters) and added interior measurements and floor plans in 2022, so it now describes itself as serving both exterior and interior trades.

In January 2026 Hover relaunched its product as one connected platform covering measurements, 2D and 3D design, automated estimating from the 3D model, homeowner proposals with e-signature, and what it says are more than 1,000 integrations with CRM, production and business systems. Its Instant Design tool, launched in 2025, creates photo-realistic design options from a single photo using products from manufacturers such as James Hardie, GAF and Pella.

Hover was founded in 2011 and is based in San Francisco. It said in 2020 that it had raised $147 million, including a $60 million round led by insurers Travelers, State Farm Ventures and Nationwide, and earlier investors include GV and The Home Depot. Hover says more than 300,000 contractors and home improvement professionals have used it. ABC Supply contractors can also upload blueprints for new-construction measurements and bill Hover jobs to their ABC Supply account.

The trade-off: someone has to photograph the property on site (or supply plans), and Hover's pricing page could not be checked for this review, so confirm the current plan and per-project costs with Hover before you commit.
ai_tools.how_it_works: A rep or the homeowner takes a guided set of photos of the house with the Hover app. Hover processes the photos into a measured 3D model, and for new construction ABC Supply contractors can upload blueprints instead. From the model you get measurements for ordering materials, can show the homeowner design options in 2D or 3D (including real products from manufacturers such as James Hardie, GAF and Pella), and, on the January 2026 platform, generate an estimate and a homeowner proposal with e-signature. Hover also measures interiors and produces floor plans. Data can flow into CRM and production systems through Hover's integrations.

ai_tools.long_description:
Podium is a customer-communication and lead-conversion platform for local businesses. It is owned and operated by Podium Corporation, Inc., a private company based in Lehi, Utah, and Podium says it started in 2014 as a reviews platform. Today it sells what it calls an AI Employee alongside reviews, phones, lead consolidation, website chat, a shared inbox, payments, text marketing and automations, and its site targets auto dealers, home services, aesthetics and wellness, and retail.

For home services, Podium brands its AI Employee as "Larry." Podium says Larry answers every call, handles calls, texts, web chats, email and third-party leads in one inbox, books jobs onto your dispatch board with access to your calendar, technicians and price book, sends arrival times, follows up on unpaid invoices at day 3, 7 and 14, and spots maintenance-agreement opportunities during booking conversations. Outside home services the agent is called Jerry; Podium's Jerry 2.0 case study says Podium AI runs on OpenAI's GPT-5.1.

Review requests and payments are still part of the package: Podium sends automatic review requests after jobs and offers text-to-pay and tap-to-pay. Conversion and revenue figures on its site are Podium's own claims, so judge them against your own call data.

The trade-off: Podium does not publish prices, so you only learn the cost through a sales demo, and its messaging, review and payment features overlap with what many field-service platforms already include. Map what your FSM already does and get a written quote before adding it.
ai_tools.how_it_works: You connect Podium to your phone lines, website chat and review profiles, and it pulls calls, texts, web chats, email and third-party lead sources into one inbox. Its AI Employee (Larry in the home-services version, Jerry elsewhere) responds around the clock, qualifies the customer, and, per Podium, books the job onto your dispatch board using your calendar, technicians and price book, then sends arrival times and follows up on leads. After the job, Podium requests a review automatically and can collect payment by text-to-pay or tap-to-pay, with automatic reminders on unpaid balances. ai_tools.long_description:
Birdeye is a reputation and customer-experience platform for local and multi-location businesses, run by Birdeye Inc from Palo Alto, California. Its About page says brothers Naveen and Neeraj Gupta started it after a 2012 hospital stay in the family, and Birdeye says 10,000+ brands use it. The company is privately held; its 2022 Series C was led by Accel-KKR, and in 2023 it announced it had passed $100M in annual recurring revenue.

The product now centers on what Birdeye calls AI coworkers: Jay for marketing (AI search visibility, reviews, listings, social, chatbot and marketing automation), Myna for front-desk operations (appointments, reminders and multi-channel messaging), and Robin for customer experience (surveys, insights, competitor analysis, ticketing and reporting). Its home-services page adds referral campaigns and digital payments, and Birdeye says 9,000+ home-service businesses and contractors use it.

For a trades business, the core is review generation: Birdeye says it integrates with over 3,000 software systems, including ServiceTitan, Housecall Pro, JobNimbus, Service Fusion, QuickBooks and Square, so review requests can be triggered from the software you already use, and its Review Response Agent drafts replies in your brand voice and either posts them or holds them for approval.

The trade-off: Birdeye does not publish prices, its pitch is aimed at multi-location brands, and the full suite is more than a one-truck shop needs. It also overlaps with review and messaging features in many FSM platforms and in tools like Podium, so decide which system owns reviews and messaging before you buy.
ai_tools.how_it_works: You connect Birdeye to your Google Business Profile and other listings, and to the software you already run, such as ServiceTitan, Housecall Pro, JobNimbus, Service Fusion, QuickBooks or Square. Birdeye's review agent asks customers for reviews, pulls incoming reviews into one dashboard, and drafts responses that post automatically or wait for your approval. The same platform handles listings, social posting, web chat and texting, appointment reminders, surveys, referral campaigns and digital payments, organized around its AI coworkers (Jay for marketing, Myna for front-desk operations, Robin for customer experience). Pricing is quoted: you fill in a form with your number of locations and Birdeye's team comes back with a price.

Sameday (legal name Sameday AI Inc.) sells what it calls "the AI front office for home services": AI customer-service reps that answer calls, book jobs into your field-service software and run outbound follow-up. Its About page says it was founded in 2022 by Aaron Cooper and Max Forsey, two home-service operators with pest control and roofing backgrounds, and its Y Combinator profile lists it in the Winter 2023 batch, based in Lehi, Utah. The old gosameday.com address now redirects to sameday.ai.

The AI CSRs answer calls, schedule through a booking tool Sameday calls the Scheduling Wizard, send texts, and follow playbooks that can pitch financing and membership plans. Campaigns run outbound reactivation, follow-ups and member outreach, a Coach feature analyzes call performance, and the phone system handles routing and queues. Sameday names ServiceTitan (as a certified app), Housecall Pro, FieldRoutes, AccuLynx and JobNimbus among its integrations, plus lead sources such as Thumbtack, Google Local Services, Angi and Facebook. You keep your business number and forward calls to a number Sameday provides.

When a call comes in, an AI CSR answers, qualifies the caller, books the appointment against your real schedule and can follow playbooks for financing or membership offers. ai_tools.long_description:
Routific is route-optimization and delivery-management software from Routific Solutions Inc., which its co-founder Marc Kuo started in 2012 and which news coverage places in Vancouver, British Columbia. Routific pitches itself at last-mile delivery businesses (food and meal delivery, couriers, grocery, florists, furniture), not field service, but its routing engine can plan any day of stops, and its free plan makes it a low-risk way for a small trades crew to test whether optimized routes save drive time.

Every plan, including the free one, gets route optimization, unlimited drivers, unlimited dispatchers, driver mobile apps, real-time GPS tracking, email customer notifications, a customer-facing Delivery Tracker and proof of delivery. SMS notifications are a paid add-on and are not included on the free plan.

Pricing is by order volume, not by driver: free up to 100 orders a month, $150/mo for 101-1,000, then an added per-order charge that falls from 15 cents to 3 cents as volume rises, with custom pricing above 50,000 orders. Routific counts each order once, when it is scheduled to a route. Its named integrations are e-commerce systems (Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento, BigCommerce, Zoho) plus an API and webhooks.

The trade-off: Routific is a delivery-routing tool, not an FSM. It does no quoting, invoicing or CRM, names no field-service software integrations, and its proof-of-delivery and delivery-tracker features are built around drop-offs rather than service calls. Treat it as a routing layer you test on the free plan alongside your existing software.
ai_tools.how_it_works: You import or enter your stops (addresses, time windows and other constraints), and Routific's optimization engine plans routes across your drivers. Drivers follow the route in the mobile app, which tracks them by GPS and captures proof of delivery, while customers get email notifications and a Delivery Tracker link. Orders can come in by hand, by file, from e-commerce integrations such as Shopify, or through Routific's API and webhooks. Billing counts each order once, when it is scheduled to a route: free up to 100 a month, $150/mo up to 1,000, then a per-order charge that steps down with volume. ai_tools.long_description:
NiceJob is review and reputation-marketing software for small service businesses. It began as a Vancouver startup, was acquired in October 2021 by Paystone, a Canadian payments company, and its website now lists NiceJob Inc. at Paystone's London, Ontario address, with its privacy and careers pages hosted on paystone.com. NiceJob says it has served 50K+ businesses across home services, auto and moving, beauty and wellness, and professional services.

The product is built around review requests. The Starter plan ($75/mo) sends review requests by SMS and email, shows your reviews in website widgets, shares them to social media, and adds a team leaderboard and a reviews microsite. Pro ($125/mo) adds rebooking reminders, referral campaigns, email broadcasts, AI-generated review replies, customer gifts, NPS surveys and competitor monitoring. A managed website (Sites) costs $99/mo plus a $199 setup fee. There is a 14-day free trial and no contract.

The AI is focused: AI Replies on Pro drafts responses to reviews, and an AI Leads add-on for lead qualification is listed as coming soon without a price. NiceJob names integrations with Jobber, Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan, QuickBooks, Square, Stripe, HubSpot and FreshBooks, plus Zapier, so review requests can go out automatically when a job closes.

Ownership is the thing to watch. Paystone and related companies entered court-supervised creditor protection (CCAA) in Ontario in June 2026, and on August 27, 2026 the court approved a sale of their business and assets to a company controlled by Paystone's principals; the monitor reported in mid-September that closing was still pending. The filings describe a reputation-marketing software line without naming NiceJob. The trade-off: NiceJob is a focused, month-to-month review tool at a published price, narrower than Podium or Birdeye, and its parent is mid-restructuring, so avoid prepaying far ahead.
ai_tools.how_it_works: You connect NiceJob to your Google Business Profile and to the software you already use (NiceJob names Jobber, Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan, QuickBooks, Square, Stripe, HubSpot and FreshBooks, plus Zapier). When a job is completed or paid, NiceJob sends the customer a review request by SMS and email and guides them to leave a review, then shows those reviews in widgets on your website and shares them to social media. On Pro, it also sends rebooking reminders and referral campaigns, drafts AI replies to reviews, runs NPS surveys and email broadcasts, and monitors competitors. Pricing is a flat $75/mo (Starter) or $125/mo (Pro), with a 14-day free trial and no contract.

ai_tools.long_description:
More Good Reviews (MGR) is a review-request and reputation tool for local and service businesses, sold with published per-location pricing. Its AppSumo listing names Scott Vayner as founder and gives New York, New York and July 2022 as its location and founding date. The core loop is conventional: scheduled email and SMS review requests with up to three reminders, branded review pages with QR codes and a kiosk mode, Google review sync with replies from the dashboard (Facebook Page sync was added in June 2026), AI-drafted replies that can post automatically after a set delay, website widgets, and a white-label agency portal with client single sign-on.

What sets it apart is its MCP server. From Claude or another MCP client you sign in per project, grant read, write or delete scopes, and then check reviews, look up customers, schedule requests and pull reports by asking your assistant. MGR's changelog says it went live in Claude's connector directory in August 2026, and it publishes three free Claude Agent Skills on GitHub (a reputation report, reputation actions and a review pipeline).

Its compliance documentation is specific. The Google Review Guidelines page cites the FTC's Consumer Reviews and Testimonials rule and warns against review gating and paying for reviews. The link revealer, which keeps a public review option open for customers who give a low rating, shows by default, and the docs warn that blocking public reviews can get listings removed. AI Review Suggestions is off by default and the docs tell customers to edit suggestions to match their experience, but the feature still takes keywords in its settings, so we would leave it off. The SMS Consent page explains prior express written consent and says TextLink's phone-based setup does not remove the need for consent.

The trade-off: MGR is a young, founder-led company that also sells an AppSumo lifetime deal, and ongoing sync covers only Google and Facebook; Yelp, Trustpilot, LinkedIn and other sites are one-time imports. It names no field-service software integrations (customers come in by CSV, Stripe, HubSpot, Zapier or API).
ai_tools.how_it_works: You connect your Google Business Profile (and Facebook Page), import customers by CSV, Stripe, HubSpot, Zapier or the API, and set a request strategy: when email and SMS review requests go out and up to three reminders. SMS goes through your own Twilio, ClickSend, SimpleTexting or TextLink account, so texting costs are yours, and STOP replies unsubscribe customers when the incoming webhook is set up. Customers land on a branded review page with a star rating; low ratings see a feedback form plus a link revealer that keeps a public review option visible by default (leave it on; hiding it is the gating pattern Google prohibits). Google reviews sync about every four hours, and AI can draft replies or post them automatically after a delay you choose. Agencies get a separate white-label portal with per-client projects, SSO and an agency-level MCP server. For AI assistants, you add the project's MCP URL in Claude or another MCP client, sign in, grant scopes, and manage requests, reviews and reports conversationally.

pros_detail.title: Published pricing with a no-card trial
pros_detail.explanation: MGR's pricing page lists Business from $59 per location/month ($49 billed yearly) with 5,000 requests per location, and a $99/month Agency plan, with a 7-day free trial and no card required. Podium and Birdeye, by contrast, publish no prices.

pros_detail.title: An MCP server and Claude skills
pros_detail.explanation: You can manage reviews, customers, requests and reports from Claude or any MCP client, with per-project sign-in and read, write or delete scopes. MGR says it is listed in Claude's connector directory and publishes free Claude Agent Skills on GitHub.

ai_faqs.a: Asking customers for reviews is fine; what Google prohibits is gating (sending only happy customers to public reviews), and the FTC rule bans buying reviews and suppressing negative ones. MGR's link revealer keeps a public review path open by default, incentives are optional and off unless you add them, and AI Review Suggestions is off by default with docs telling customers to edit any suggestion. ai_tools.long_description:
Rooftops AI is run by Mutter Voice, LLC, a Tennessee limited liability company doing business as Rooftops AI, according to its terms of service. It started as a satellite roof-measurement tool and now sells what it calls the AI that runs your roofing company: instant roof reports, a CRM and inbox with text and email follow-up, a website built from your Google listing, an AI Front Desk phone line that answers calls 24/7, and door-knock tracking on a map. Rooftops AI says it has generated 15,000+ reports and serves hundreds of roofers.

Reports are built from high-resolution satellite imagery combined with Google's 3D elevation data. Each one gives area, pitch, facet count and squares including waste, a cost estimate and a one-click proposal, plus NWS-verified hail and wind history for the address. Every report carries a confidence score, and complex or tree-covered roofs are flagged for on-site verification. The company says it covers addresses in all 50 states where high-resolution imagery exists.

Pricing is published. Billed yearly, AIReports is $39/mo for 30 reports a month, AIPro $79/mo for 100 reports plus the website, CRM, crews and invoicing, AIEmployee $159/mo for unlimited reports and a phone line with 500 minutes, and AIUnlimited $399/mo with three seats and 1,500 minutes; monthly billing costs 20% more. A free account includes three full reports with no card.

The caution is what is not published. Rooftops AI gives no margin of error or accuracy percentage, does not say how current its imagery is, and does not mention Xactimate or insurance-carrier acceptance. Its own terms say users "must independently verify measurements, product identifications, and estimates (including by on-site inspection) before relying on them for bids, contracts, material orders, insurance claims, or any other business or legal purpose."

The trade-off: it is a fast, low-cost first-pass measurement and proposal tool with a growing office suite around it, but insurance and supplement work still needs on-site verification, and plan names are in flux (the homepage FAQ still describes Pro at $99/mo and a Front Desk plan at $199/mo), so confirm the current plan before you commit.

Every report includes a confidence score, and complex or tree-covered roofs are flagged for on-site verification. Higher plans wrap an office around the reports: a CRM and inbox for website, phone and storm leads, text and email follow-up sequences, a website on your own domain with an instant estimate form, crews and invoicing on AIPro, and on AIEmployee and AIUnlimited an AI phone line that answers every call within a monthly minute allowance.
